summary: 3DNow!-intrinsic composition of a 4x4 transformation matrix from up to six optional packed-float inputs. Reads rotation/axis data from a3/a4, optionally applies translation from a2, optionally post-multiplies an a6 rotation and subtracts an a5 translation, then optionally adds an a7 translation; every null input falls back to an identity component. The inverse-rotation product algorithm (pfadd/pfmul/pfsub/punpck on 0x3F8000003F800000 and 1065353216 constants) is the same as sub_522B5B. Returns the output matrix pointer a1.

local_names.a1: output 4x4 transformation matrix (8 __m64 slots, two floats per row)
local_names.a2: optional translation vector (packed pair a2[0], a2[1])
local_names.a3: optional rotation source (packed pair a3[0], a3[1]) whose inverse rotation is computed
local_names.a4: optional rotation parameter/axis data (packed pair a4[0], a4[1])
local_names.a5: optional translation vector subtracted when present
local_names.a6: optional post-multiplication rotation (packed pair a6[0], a6[1])

operations.description: If a4 is null, no rotation source exists: initialize the output to identity.
Identity fallback: write a1[0] = 1.0f (0x3F800000), a1[1] = 0, a1[2] = packed 1.0/1.0, a1[3] = 0, a1[4] = 0, a1[5] = 1.0f, a1[6] = 0, a1[7] = packed 1.0/1.0, filling every output matrix slot.

If a4 is present but a3 is null, build a rotation matrix from a4 alone: a1[0] = a4[0] low half, a1[2] = a4[0] high half, a1[5] = a4[1] low float, a1[7] = 0x3F80000000000000 (packed 1.0/1.0), with the remaining slots zeroed.
If both a4 and a3 are present, build the full 3x3 inverse rotation from the a3/a4 packed data.

Compute the inverse-rotation products from a3/a4 using pfadd, pfmul, pfsub/pfsubr, pfacc and punpck intrinsics against the packed constant 0x3F8000003F800000 (1.0/1.0) and 1065353216 (1.0f), staging the rotation row components into stack buffers v377..v401.

The packet's fact table flags three read-only globals as read by this function (qword_5AF8E0, qword_5AF8F0, qword_5AF900); the raw decompilation renders their values as inline literals (0x3F800000 identity, 0x3F8000003F800000 packed 1.0/1.0, 1065353216), so the exact global-to-constant mapping is not established.
Inside the a3/a4 rotation path: if a2 is non-null, apply a2 as a translation and compose the full matrix.

a2-present path: stage identity+translation from a2 (a1[0]=1.0f, a1[1]=0, a1[2]=packed 1.0/1.0, a1[5]=1.0f, a1[6]=-a2[0], a1[7]=packed (1.0f - a2[1])), then read back matrix rows a1[0..7] while accumulating the 4x4 multiply into every output slot.
a2-null path: store the pure rotation matrix rows a1[0..7] (translation and homogeneous slots left as the rotation-composed values).
If a6 is non-null, post-multiply the accumulated matrix by a second rotation built from a6.
Build the a6 rotation using the same inverse-rotation product sequence (pfadd, pfmul, pfsubr, pfacc against 0x3F8000003F800000, 1065353216) staged in stack buffers v381..v393.
Inside the a6 path: if a5 is non-null, subtract a5 as a translation before composing.
a5-present path: subtract a5 from the output translation slots (result[6] -= a5[0], result[7].low-int32 -= a5[1] float), then accumulate the 4x4 multiply across the output matrix rows.
a5-null path: compose the a6 rotation into the output matrix rows without a translation adjustment.
If a7 is non-null, add a7 as a final translation.
Add a7 into the output translation slots: result[6] += a7[0] and result[7].low-int32 += a7[1] float.
Execute _m_femms() to exit MMX state and return the output matrix pointer a1.
